result.rationale: The diff's update path is `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, and PostRevisor#revise! as shown takes only (user, new_raw, opts) — no title is ever passed or updated. So when content_sha1 changes, only the post body is revised and the topic title stays stale, exactly as the finding describes. This is real behavior introduced by the diff and a genuine data-freshness defect for feed-imported topics whose headlines change.

judged_text: The update path revises only the post body — `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` passes no title — so the topic title is written once at creation and never again. When a source article's headline changes (routine for news/editorial feeds), the content updates but the topic keeps the stale title forever, and the schema/model offers no way to express a title update.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path sets the title via `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, ...)`, but the update path only calls `PostRevisor#revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)`, whose signature in the diff is `revise!(user, new_raw, opts = {})` and updates only `@post.raw` (and then saves). No title/topic-title update is performed on change (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). This means updated feed/article headlines would not be reflected after initial creation—an incomplete synchronization concern rather than a strictly broken behavior proven wrong by the diff.
